name: Earth
subject: An angular ochre chunk of mineral matter with exposed dark strata and a few dense crumbs, isolated against ultramarine. Its solid, weighty silhouette stands for the primal power of matter.

name: Air
subject: Three broad ivory ribbons of moving air curl around a clear central opening, with a few tiny wind-carried grains at the outer turn. Leave most of the circle open.

name: Fire
subject: One compact coral flame with a pale hot heart and two broad upward tongues, hovering in darkness without logs or a hearth.

name: Water
subject: One heavy jade-blue droplet leans into a short curling pool, with a clear pale highlight and deep transparent belly.

name: Light
subject: A single brilliant ivory point releases a broad diagonal beam through ultramarine darkness; the beam visibly opens into empty space.

name: Dust
subject: A loose diagonal spray of small dry ochre grains and uneven flakes, with individual particles separated by dark space.

name: Mist
subject: A low, translucent jade-white veil folds into two soft overlapping wisps, with dark background still visible through its body.

name: Gravity
subject: Three unequal rocky spheres lie along narrowing curved paths toward one larger dark sphere; the nearest small sphere is visibly closest to the large mass. Keep the paths fine and the masses prominent.

name: Dense cloud
subject: A compact indigo and jade cosmic cloud has a very dark dense knot at its centre and pale granular edges folded inward. No star shines inside it yet.

name: First star
subject: One white-blue spherical star shines alone in a nearly empty ultramarine field, with a restrained pale halo and no flame-like surface.

name: Starfield
subject: A loose irregular scatter of separate ivory and warm-white stars occupies the circle, with clear dark gaps and no connecting lines.

name: Galaxy
subject: A tilted spiral galaxy has two broad luminous arms, granular star clouds, dark dust lanes and a small bright central bulge.

name: Massive star
subject: An enormous blue-white stellar disk fills most of the circle, its intensely bright limb surrounded by a thick hot halo. Preserve the rounded surface and avoid tongues of fire.

name: Fusing core
subject: A cutaway of a luminous star exposes a small white central core nested inside three broad coral and ochre shells, with tiny paired grains becoming denser clusters in the innermost shell.

name: Supernova
subject: A fierce white central flash throws broad coral ejecta fingers outward in every direction, with torn stellar layers visibly separating from the centre.

name: Heavy elements
subject: Within a dark cutaway wedge of stellar material, several compact clusters of ivory, coral and metallic ochre grains sit tightly packed, enclosed by a curved glowing stellar shell. This is an atlas convention for heavier nuclei still inside a star.

name: Expanding remnant
subject: A broad hollow shell of ragged coral gas surrounds a dark evacuated centre, with sparse fragments continuing outward beyond its rim. The initial blinding flash has passed.

name: Glowing nebula
subject: Filmy jade and coral gas folds glow across a dark central opening, edged with delicate ivory light and a few embedded points. The cloud is thin and luminous rather than solid.

name: Enriched dust
subject: A diagonal cloud of fine dark grains contains larger ochre, coral and pale metallic flecks, all dispersed freely against deep blue. Several flecks show distinct bright edges.

name: New stellar nursery
subject: Three compact white-gold star embryos glow inside separate dense folds of one large jade and ultramarine cloud, with fine ochre grains gathered around them.

name: Sun
subject: A warm ochre sun with a pale circular face and a short clean corona floats in dark blue space; its disk is calm and complete.

name: Planetary disk
subject: A small golden sun sits inside a broad flat tilted disk of dusty ochre rings, with a clear central opening and scattered clumps along the disk.

name: Planetesimals
subject: Four irregular rocky bodies of different sizes tumble together in empty blue space; the largest has a rough cratered edge and none is spherical.

name: Rocky world
subject: A solid round young planet has a dark ochre surface with the same hook-shaped raised landmass and two small satellite ridges used throughout this world, against deep blue space. No familiar Earth continent is present.

name: Magma ocean
subject: The same round planet glows coral across most of its surface; a few dark cooling rafts outline the hooked landmass as cracks of bright molten rock divide them.

name: Iron core
subject: A rocky planet is cut open to show a dense ochre-metal inner sphere surrounded by a broad coral liquid-metal layer and a thinner dark rocky mantle.

name: Magnetic field
subject: The recurring dark planet is enclosed by two large symmetric jade field loops that leave one pole and curve back to the other, with a few solar particles diverted around the outside.

name: Stone crust
subject: A broad curved slab of dark solid rock shows a cool cracked upper surface and a thin coral glow beneath its cut edge, suggesting a hardened skin over a hot interior.

name: Aurora
subject: Tall jade and pale-coral curtains hang above a dark curved polar horizon, their lower edges rippling while a few small stars remain visible overhead.

name: Giant impact
subject: An oblique small rocky body strikes the rim of the recurring large planet, sending a white-coral fan of debris into a curved orbit while most of the planet remains intact.

name: Moon
subject: A pale ivory moon combines a clearly lit crescent with its faint round unlit body; two neighboring circular craters sit near the lit lower edge. Retain that crater pair in every close Moon view.

name: Tides
subject: The hooked shore appears in miniature under the pale Moon; two broad nested waterlines show the sea at high and low positions against the same rock.

name: First rain
subject: Large bright raindrops fall from a low grey-white cloud onto cool, solid grey stone, making pale splashes and small dark wet patches on its closed, unlit cracks. All land is bare mineral rock; there is no molten lava, fire, orange glow or vegetation.

name: Rain-filled hollows
subject: Three irregular shallow basins in bare dark stone hold separate jade pools beneath the last few raindrops; raised dry rock clearly divides the pools.

name: Ocean
subject: A broad uninterrupted ultramarine sea curves toward a quiet pale horizon, with one deep jade foreground swell and no visible islands or living shore.

name: Tidal shore
subject: A shallow jade sea recedes from a solid unbroken hooked ochre-grey cliff, exposing a broad wet mineral shelf dotted with small tide pools. The cliff has no cave, arch or opening, and every exposed land surface is bare rock or sediment without green tufts, grass, roots or trees.

name: Evaporation
subject: A warm ochre sun illuminates a shallow sea, where thin transparent streams rise from the surface and fade into clear air before forming any cloud.

name: Clouds
subject: Two substantial ivory cumulus clouds stack softly above a flat dark lower edge, with cool jade shadows and a few pale gaps between the lobes.

name: Rainfall
subject: A broad grey-jade cloud releases a visible curtain of slanting pale drops onto a bare ochre-grey mineral hillside and a small jade stream. Smooth rock slopes, loose sediment and rain-darkened stone carry no green tufts, grass, roots, moss or trees.

name: Rivers
subject: One strong jade river winds from high grey hills across bare ochre mineral land, fed by two narrow tributaries that merge into its single channel. Exposed banks and hills consist entirely of rock, gravel and sediment, with no green tufts, grass, roots or trees.

name: Sediment
subject: A low fan of sorted ochre sand, pale pebbles and dark fine silt lies in shallow water, with visibly separate coarse and fine bands along its edge.

name: Delta
subject: A jade river splits into three outward-reaching channels across a triangular ochre sediment fan at the edge of a dark blue sea. Every bar, bank and upstream slope is bare ochre-grey mineral material, with no green tufts, grass, roots, marsh plants or trees.

name: Rainbow
subject: One bright but restrained multicolored bow arcs between a sunlit cloud edge and a slanting rain shower, with dark blue space inside the curve.

name: Water cycle
subject: A compact island cross-section shows a sunlit sea, a cloud above a bare grey-ochre mountain and a jade river returning to the same sea, joined by one pale sweeping loop rising on the sea side and descending over land. Every above-water surface is exposed rock or sediment, without green tufts, grass, roots or trees.

name: Moving plates
subject: Two thick dark crustal slabs meet in cutaway: one bends downward beneath the other while a coral seam opens at the far side. Broad pale motion strokes follow the slabs.

name: Continent
subject: A broad ochre landmass with the world's distinctive hook-shaped cape stretches across a jade sea, its inland ridges low and its coastline continuous.

name: Trench
subject: A side cutaway beneath a continuous blue ocean shows a narrow seafloor trough where the left rocky plate bends downward and continues diagonally beneath the neighboring right plate. Keep the descending slab visibly continuous below its neighbor within solid ochre-grey mantle, with only a narrow water-filled surface depression rather than a giant open fissure.

name: Volcano
subject: A steep dark volcanic cone releases a compact coral eruption and a short glowing lava stream down one flank, with an exposed crater at the summit.

name: Hydrothermal vent
subject: Two rough dark mineral chimneys rise from the deep seafloor, releasing thick black plumes into jade water; small pale mineral edges catch the faint light.

name: Weathered rock
subject: A large ochre rock is split by water-darkened cracks, with rounded corners, detached chips and a short rivulet carrying fine grains away from its base.

name: Mineral-rich sea
subject: At a rocky coast, a jade river plume fans into blue sea carrying a few bright mineral grains that grow smaller and fade into the water. Show the moving water and mineral source together.

name: Volcanic island
subject: A bare dark volcanic island rises from a broad blue sea, with a small ochre crater and fresh black lava slopes reaching directly into the water.

name: Organic molecules
subject: Several irregular chains and small loops of joined ochre, ivory and coral grains drift in dark jade water beside one mineral surface. Use a hand-painted microscopic atlas convention, without letters, bonds as technical diagrams or equipment.

name: Membranes
subject: Two thin translucent jade bubbles float in dark water, each with a clear double-edged boundary enclosing nearly empty fluid; one open curved sheet is folding toward closure.

name: Chemical fuel
subject: A small cluster of tightly joined coral and ochre molecular grains catches a narrow shaft of sunlight, with warm light retained in the cluster after the beam passes. Keep a few unlit grains nearby for contrast.

name: Living cell
subject: One large soft jade cell has a clearly bounded outer membrane and a few small internal coral threads and grains suspended in fluid. Keep the interior simple, with no prominent nucleus.

name: Dividing cells
subject: Two matching jade cell lobes pinch apart through a narrow connecting waist, each containing the same small coral thread-and-grain pattern.

name: Variation
subject: Four related jade cells form a loose branching family, sharing the same basic boundary but differing slightly in size and in the arrangement of their coral internal threads.

name: Sun-fed cells
subject: Three jade-green cells lie close beneath a warm shaft of sunlight, their interiors filled with small leaf-green granules; a few pale bubbles leave the group.

name: Microbial mats
subject: A low emerald and ochre living film coats a flat wet rock, shown with one cut edge revealing several thin soft layers; tiny bubbles sit along its surface.

name: Stromatolites
subject: Three rounded low domes rise in shallow water, their cutaway sides revealing closely stacked wavy ochre and jade laminae beneath a thin living green surface.

name: Oxygen
subject: Several pale paired spheres rise as bubbles from a small green microbial patch in water, with one pair enlarged near the foreground. The repeated pair is a simple atlas convention for oxygen.

name: Rusted seabed
subject: A shallow seabed is stained with broad coral-red and dark ochre deposits, with a thin greenish water layer and a few settling pale particles above it.

name: Banded iron
subject: A broken upright slab exposes bold alternating dark iron-grey and coral-red horizontal bands, with a rough outer edge and a small wet seabed base.

name: Oxygen-rich sky
subject: The familiar hooked continent curves beneath a broad clear pale-blue atmospheric band, containing a few paired ivory gas marks well above the sea.

name: Ozone layer
subject: A thin luminous jade shell lies high above the familiar curved planet, with three-part pale gas clusters and several short incoming violet light rays fading at the shell.

name: Oxygen-using cells
subject: One pale jade cell draws paired ivory gas marks inward beside a separate small ochre food grain; its simple interior shows a warm coral glow.

name: Partnered cells
subject: A large translucent jade host cell encloses one clearly distinct small coral oval partner with a folded internal line; both retain visible boundaries.

name: Sheltered microbes
subject: A lifted corner of a thick green microbial mat reveals a dark sealed pocket in the underlying mud, containing several tiny pale cells protected beneath the living surface.

name: Cell colonies
subject: A loose rosette of eight visibly separate jade cells touches edge to edge, each cell retaining its own outline and simple interior.

name: Multicellular life
subject: A simple rounded ribbon-shaped body is assembled from two visibly different sizes of connected cells, with one continuous outer contour and a hollow central passage.

name: Algae
subject: A small rooted-looking but unattached cluster of jade and olive seaweed fronds grows from a rough submerged stone; broad translucent blades bend underwater.

name: Soft-bodied animals
subject: A translucent oval marine animal with a gently lobed edge rests beside a slender worm-like companion; both have soft continuous bodies without hard shells or jointed legs.

name: Swimming animals
subject: A streamlined small marine animal swims diagonally, propelled by broad side fins and a clearly flexed tail, with a simple head and no emphasized eye.

name: Eyes
subject: A close view of a small marine animal's head gives one large dark eye a bright highlight, while a narrow shaft of light reaches the eye from above.

name: Shells
subject: Two hard pale marine shells sit against deep jade water: one strong spiral and one ribbed fan shape, both visibly hollow at the opening.

name: Fossils
subject: A split ochre stone slab reveals a sharply outlined spiral-shell impression and a small ribbed shell trace embedded in the rock.

name: Kelp forest
subject: Three tall ochre-jade kelp stems rise from dark submerged rocks, bearing long ribbon blades and a few round gas floats beneath a pale water surface.

name: Coral
subject: One small colony of pale coral polyps attaches to a submerged stone, each polyp an open cup with a short crown of tentacles.

name: Reef partnership
subject: One enlarged coral polyp shows a pale translucent body containing several small jade-green cells; its tentacles remain spread above a rough attachment stone.

name: Coral reef
subject: A compact underwater reef combines several sturdy branching and mound-shaped pale coral skeletons, with tiny living coral tips and deep blue gaps between the structures.

name: Nursery waters
subject: Three tiny jade juvenile swimmers shelter within a protective arch of large ochre kelp blades, their small bodies sharply silhouetted in a calm dark gap.

name: Coastal mosaic
subject: An oblique strip of solid unbroken hooked ochre-grey coast contains separate cool dark kelp coves and warmer pale coral shallows, divided by bare rocky headlands and connected by blue water. All green kelp and algae remain visibly underwater; exposed land has no green tufts, grass, roots or trees, and the cliff has no cave or arch.

name: Living coast
subject: The solid unbroken hooked ochre-grey coast holds a submerged kelp cove, separate underwater coral shallows and a broad bare tidal shelf; one sweeping jade tidal current connects the habitats around the cape. Green life is confined to visibly underwater kelp and algae, while all exposed land remains mineral without green tufts, grass, roots, trees, cave or arch.

name: Waves
subject: Three broad jade ocean swells approach in diagonal succession, the nearest curling into a clear ivory breaking crest over dark water.

name: Sea cave
subject: A close oblique view of the same hooked cliff shows a dark wave-cut entrance at water level, a sloping dry upper ledge and a pale unmarked inner wall above the wash.

name: Shore plants
subject: Small upright green shoots and flat primitive-looking leaflets occupy wet cracks just above a jade shoreline, with algae still visible below the waterline.

name: Soil
subject: A compact cutaway of dark crumbly topsoil shows pale fine roots, decomposed leaf fragments and scattered mineral grains beneath a thin green surface.

name: Windblown spores
subject: Fine pale spore grains blow from a small open capsule on a slender green stalk, spreading into a broad tapering trail above low wet growth.

name: Moss
subject: A dense low cushion of bright jade moss carries several fine upright stalks with tiny brown capsules, rooted against a wet dark stone.

name: Wetland
subject: A shallow dark pool lies among low mossy hummocks and saturated ochre ground, with several small patches of standing water connected below the growth.

name: Roots
subject: One sturdy green stem ends in a spreading fan of pale branching roots, revealed in a dark soil cutaway with fine rootlets reaching toward water pockets.

name: Ferns
subject: Two large jade fern fronds unfurl above a small dark root mass; one curled fiddlehead stands beside a fully opened divided frond.

name: First forest
subject: Three tall primitive tree-fern-like trunks rise from wet ground into spreading divided jade crowns, with low ferns beneath and no flowers, fruit or animals.

name: Fallen wood
subject: One thick broken dark branch lies diagonally, its pale torn end and a few attached bark strips clearly visible against a small patch of leaf litter.

name: Fungi
subject: A small group of ochre and ivory mushrooms grows from a dark fallen branch, with pale threadlike mycelium exposed beneath one lifted bark edge.

name: Decomposition
subject: A broken log crumbles into dark fibrous fragments beneath pale fungal threads and two small mushroom caps; the intact end transitions visibly into loose organic matter.

name: Returned nutrients
subject: Small ochre and pale mineral flecks emerge from dark decomposed leaf fragments and gather beside fine roots in moist soil, following a short pale flow through the cutaway.

name: Renewing forest
subject: Small new fern trees with splayed divided fronds grow among taller trunks of the same early fern forest, their roots reaching into rich soil beside old naturally snapped and splintered trunks and decaying wood. Every broken trunk has an irregular torn end, with no flat saw-cut stump, axe marks, tools or broadleaf sapling replacing the fern family.

name: Peat
subject: A cutaway of saturated dark brown ground exposes thick soft layers of recognizable pressed stems and leaves beneath a shallow mossy pool.

name: Buried carbon
subject: A deep dark carbon-rich layer containing faint compressed plant traces lies beneath several thick ochre sediment beds and far below a small green surface.

name: Forest rain
subject: The same tall early fern forest raises straight trunks into a canopy of splayed, clearly divided jade fronds; fine pale moisture wisps rise from that canopy into a low cloud that rains over the far edge of the forest. Keep the frond crowns distinct rather than replacing them with rounded flowering or broadleaf tree canopies.

name: Arthropods
subject: A dark ochre many-segmented shoreline animal has a clear external armored back, antennae and several pairs of visibly jointed legs.

name: Insects
subject: One broad-bodied ochre insect stands in side-three-quarter view with exactly six clearly separated legs, two antennae and three main body regions; wings are folded or absent.

name: Winged insects
subject: A slim dragonfly-like insect spreads two pairs of translucent jade-veined wings above a six-legged body and long segmented abdomen.

name: Canopy life
subject: Three small six-legged winged insects move between broad leaves and branching twigs high above a barely visible forest floor, forming a lively horizontal band.

name: Air-breathing fish
subject: A broad-finned fish raises its mouth above the surface of a shallow reedless pool, its scaled body and fleshy paired fins still submerged among roots.

name: Limbed vertebrates
subject: A low long-tailed early tetrapod braces on four broad fleshy limbs at a muddy water margin, with splayed digits and a smooth continuous back.

name: Shelled egg
subject: A pale oval egg rests on dry ochre ground, with a clean small cutaway revealing protective membranes and a curled embryo inside; keep the shell otherwise whole.

name: Reptiles
subject: A medium dark-ochre lizard-like reptile stands firmly on four scaled limbs with a long tapering tail, dry ridged skin and a low angular head.

name: Birds
subject: A small ochre-and-jade feathered bird perches on a bare twig with one wing partly open, showing layered flight feathers, a short beak and two feet.

name: Great browsers
subject: Two enormous sauropod-like plant eaters have long rising necks, small heads, barrel bodies, pillar legs and long tails; the nearer one strips foliage beside a tiny tree. An alternating paired trail combines large oval hind prints with smaller clawless horseshoe-shaped foreprints in the damp ground.

name: Small furred animals
subject: Two small shrew-like mammals with pointed noses, round ears, long tails and fine ochre fur shelter beside a large fallen branch; their bodies remain alert and intact.

name: Flowers
subject: Three simple coral and ochre flowers open on a leafy green stem, with broad petals and visible central pollen-bearing structures. Avoid a cut bouquet or decorative vase.

name: Pollination
subject: One six-legged ochre insect bridges two open coral flowers, with a few visible pale pollen grains on its body and on the second flower's centre.

name: Seeds
subject: Three plump ochre seeds lie together, one split to reveal a pale curled plant embryo and its stored food beneath a dark protective coat.

name: Seedling
subject: One fresh jade seedling rises from a cracked ochre seed, showing two broad cotyledons above a short stem and a single fine root below.

name: Windborne seeds
subject: Three recognizable ochre seeds carry broad pale papery wings as they spiral away from a leafy branch, each heavy seed body distinct from its wing.

name: Fruit
subject: A short living branch carries two plump coral fruits and one opened fruit showing several dark seeds inside its pale flesh.

name: Seed dispersal
subject: A small four-limbed animal carries a coral fruit away from its parent plant, while two intact dark seeds lie farther along its path on bare soil.

name: Flowering forest
subject: Three established green tree crowns carry small coral blossoms and ochre fruit above a shaded floor, with one bird and one small mammal at different branches.

name: Axial tilt
subject: The same rocky planet retains its recognizable hook-shaped ochre continent and two smaller satellite ridges, now surrounded by jade sea; a single thin ivory polar axis passes through the planet on a clear diagonal against a faint horizontal orbital plane. A small rotation arc circles one planetary pole, while the land and sea remain exposed rather than replaced by gas-giant cloud swirls.

name: Seasons
subject: Four recognizably seasonal views of the same forked branch form a loose ring around a golden Sun: fresh spring leaves, dense summer foliage, ochre autumn leaves falling and a bare snow-touched winter twig. The Sun is an ordinary clear disk with no axis, pole line or rotation arc through or around it.

name: Mountain range
subject: A continuous serrated chain of three dark ochre mountains rises in overlapping ridges, with pale high peaks and a deep shadowed valley between them.

name: Rain shadow
subject: One sharp mountain divides the circle: a jade cloud rains on its green windward slope while the far slope is bare ochre beneath clear sky; a thin air ribbon passes over the summit.

name: Desert
subject: Broad ochre dunes curve around a patch of cracked stony ground beneath a small white sun, with deep indigo shadows and no water or green plants.

name: Oasis
subject: A small jade spring-fed pool sits within ochre desert rock, ringed by several dense green shrubs and one spreading tree. The surrounding land remains dry.

name: Grassland
subject: A broad stand of tall ochre and jade grasses sways across gently rolling open land, with two distinct seed heads in the foreground and no tree canopy.

name: Glacier
subject: A thick pale-blue glacier descends between two dark mountain ridges, its cracked ice tongue curving toward a moraine of loose rocks.

name: Valley
subject: A wide U-shaped ochre valley lies between steep rounded walls, with scraped bare rock and a small stream on the broad flat floor; no ice remains in the foreground.

name: Braided river
subject: Several bright jade channels split and rejoin around pale gravel bars across a broad mountain valley, with cold blue headwaters visible in the distance.

name: Grazing herds
subject: Three sturdy four-legged grazing animals with short necks, modest horns and dark hoofed feet bend over open grasses, their bodies smaller than the surrounding land.

name: Scent tracking
subject: The recurring small pointed-nosed mammal lowers its nose toward a faint ochre scent trail curling along the ground from an unseen animal, with its ears lifted and body following the trail.

name: Hunting mammals
subject: Two lean furred predators with alert pointed ears, forward eyes and flexible tails move low through grass; the nearer one pauses with its muzzle close to the ground.

name: Predator and prey
subject: A lean ochre mammal pursues a darker short-necked grazer across an open strip of grass, the prey turning away while the hunter extends forward. Keep clear space between them.

name: Dung
subject: A small irregular dark-brown pile of herbivore dung rests in grass, with visible short plant fibers and a few flies kept too small to dominate.

name: Dung beetles
subject: One sturdy six-legged dark beetle pushes a round brown dung ball backward across ochre soil, its curved forelegs and hard wing cases clearly visible.

name: Fertile grassland
subject: Strong jade grass tufts rise above a dark soil cutaway where a beetle burrow and broken-down dung feed a fine pale root network.

name: Food web
subject: A compact grassland scene contains grass, a grazer, a lean hunter and a dung beetle, joined by broad unobtrusive ochre paths that return to the soil beneath the grass.

name: Watering place
subject: Two short-necked grazers drink at a shallow jade pool while a lean hunter remains partly concealed in distant grass; hoofprints mark the wet edge.

name: Far-ranging birds
subject: Three long-winged feathered birds fly above a sharp mountain saddle, their extended wings and differing distances forming one strong diagonal route.

name: Seasonal journeys
subject: Two small groups of feathered birds traverse a long pale looping route between a leafy warm branch and a snow-touched bare branch, with land and water below.

name: Island life
subject: The established volcanic island now has a modest green canopy and two perched birds separated by a broad blue sea from a distant mainland edge.

name: Different songs
subject: Two related feathered birds perch on separate island branches across a strip of sea; one sends three short pale sound arcs and the other a longer rising pair.

name: Many-voiced world
subject: The hook-marked planet carries small distinct habitat patches at its rim: a forest bird, an island bird, a grazer and a canopy insect, each with a restrained outward ripple of sound.

name: Impact winter
subject: The recurring planet is wrapped in a dark ash-grey veil that blocks most sunlight, with a small fading impact scar at its rim and a cold bare strip of land below.

name: Last tracks
subject: Exactly two alternating left-right sauropod step pairs cross grey ash-dusted wet mud and stop beneath an empty dark horizon: two large oval hind depressions each accompany a smaller clawless D-shaped foreprint, four impressions total. No living giant or approaching giant silhouette appears.

name: Fossil footprints
subject: A long tilted dry ochre stone slab preserves the same two alternating left-right sauropod step pairs as Last tracks: two large oval hind depressions and two smaller clawless D-shaped foreprints, four impressions total. A chipped layered edge and small fern establish stone and scale without crater-like raised rims.

name: Fallen forest
subject: Three broken dark tree trunks lie across grey ground beneath a dim sky, with one upright dead snag and only a tiny sheltered patch of green at the lower edge.

name: Deadwood refuge
subject: The hollow underside of a fallen trunk shelters pale fungal threads, small invertebrates and two tiny pointed-nosed mammals, with damp dark ground protected beneath the wood.

name: Small survivors
subject: The same pair of pointed-nosed, round-eared small mammals crouches in the sheltered hollow of a large broken trunk, with fungi nearby and an ash-grey clearing beyond the entrance.

name: Seed cache
subject: A shallow sheltered hollow beneath a log contains a tight cluster of intact ochre seeds; one familiar small mammal holds another seed at the entrance.

name: Green shoots
subject: Four tiny vivid jade shoots break through ash-grey soil beside a broken black branch, each emerging from a partly visible surviving seed.

name: Pioneer woodland
subject: A small uneven stand of young jade saplings grows among dark fallen logs, with mushrooms and rich soil at their roots and wide gaps between the new crowns.

name: Returning pollinators
subject: Two clearly six-legged flying insects visit coral flowers on young saplings beside an old broken trunk; the small green canopy remains open.

name: Returning fruit
subject: A young jade sapling beside a dark old stump bears a few plump coral fruits, one split enough to show seeds; a pollinating insect is small and secondary.

name: Spreading mammals
subject: Three related furred mammals spread from a deadwood shelter into young woodland: a small pointed-nosed ancestor, a sturdier ground browser and a nimble branch-climber. Maintain shared ears, fur and four-limbed anatomy.

name: Tree dwellers
subject: Two long-tailed primate-like mammals grip branching limbs with flexible hands and feet, one reaching toward a fruit while the other watches from above.

name: Whales
subject: A large streamlined jade-grey whale curves through deep water beside a smaller calf, showing horizontal tail flukes, small foreflippers and a short exhalation at the surface.

name: Bats
subject: One ochre-furred bat spreads broad dark-jade skin wings supported by long visible finger bones, with round ears, a small muzzle and two tiny hind feet.

name: New food web
subject: Young woodland holds a pollinating insect, fruiting sapling, small mammal and lean furred hunter, connected by a few curved ochre feeding paths that pass through seeds and soil.

name: Recovering world
subject: The familiar curved ochre world and hooked coastline support a mixed young forest with a small furred mammal and an insect pollinator at its living edge. Old naturally splintered, charred fallen wood remains among the different new growth as evidence of loss; no giant footprints, track depressions, fossil-track slab or living great browsers appear anywhere.

name: Snowfall
subject: Broad pale snow crystals and soft flakes fall from a cold jade-grey cloud onto the upper surface of a mountain glacier, accumulating as a fresh white cap.

name: Advancing ice
subject: A thick blue-white ice front spreads outward from high mountains across an ochre valley, burying low ridges and pushing a dark moraine before its steep cracked edge.

name: River migration
subject: A mixed line of small mammals and hoofed grazers follows a jade river downhill away from snowy peaks toward green lower country; the river remains the clear connecting route.

name: Sheltered oasis
subject: Several small mammals and a short-necked grazer gather beneath a dense green grove around a jade spring, protected by ochre rock while distant blue ice remains outside the warm enclosure.

name: Varied survivors
subject: Four members of the established small shrew-like mammal lineage stand together on neutral ground, each retaining a pointed snout, round ears, a low four-legged body and a visibly long slender tail extending beyond its rump. Their coats vary from thin through dense to softly shaggy while the body plan stays the same; thick fur has no quills, spikes or hedgehog dome.

name: Cold-adapted populations
subject: Three thick-soft-furred descendants of the same shrew-like mammals forage beside snow and low sheltering rocks, including one smaller juvenile. All retain clearly pointed snouts, round ears and visibly long slender tails beyond their thick coats, without quills, spikes, hedgehog bodies or short hidden tails.

name: Surviving lineages
subject: Two small family groups occupy adjoining habitats divided by a rock ridge: thin-furred shrew-like mammals beside a green spring and thick-soft-furred relatives beside lingering snow, each with a juvenile. Every individual retains the same pointed snout, round ears and conspicuous long slender tail, making related lineages visible across the two settings without quills or hedgehog anatomy.

name: World after the ice
subject: The same curved world retains its hook-shaped ochre land and jade water, with ice withdrawn to the far high horizon, a free-flowing river and restored woodland spreading over open lower ground among small mammals. A little old fallen wood remains within the changed forest, but no giant footprints, track depressions or living great browsers appear.

name: Attention
subject: A close profile of the established long-tailed tree dweller leans toward a bright coral fruit, its wide dark eye and lifted grasping hand aligned with the object.

name: Fear
subject: The same tree dweller crouches backward on a branch, gripping it tightly while a small lean predator silhouette appears below; the animal's eye is wide and tail drawn close.

name: Safety
subject: The tree dweller rests with a smaller companion inside a dense sheltered green grove, hidden behind interlocking branches while a distant predator passes outside the foliage.

name: Memory
subject: The tree dweller studies a familiar forked fruit branch; a faint second ivory outline of that same branch appears behind its head, while the real branch remains solid jade and coral. This double image is the recurring convention for remembered experience.

name: Learned path
subject: A single tree dweller follows an ochre path around a dark ridge toward a fruiting tree partly hidden beyond it; a faint pale trace of the same route sits under its feet.

name: Call
subject: The tree dweller opens its mouth from a high branch, releasing three broad pale sound arcs into clear air while one companion remains partly hidden behind distant leaves.

name: Shared warning
subject: One tree dweller calls from a branch while two companions turn sharply toward the same partly hidden predator; pale sound arcs link caller and listeners.

name: Social group
subject: Four established ochre-furred, long-tailed tree dwellers share a sheltered branch network as an animal family: one grooms a companion, another keeps watch and a smaller juvenile stays close. Preserve their primate faces, grasping hands and feet, full body fur and visibly curling tails; there are no humans, clothes or tools.

name: Language
subject: Two human figures in profile face one another with open speaking mouths and different deliberate hand gestures, while a third follows their shared gaze toward a small carved-free stone and the Moon.

name: Story
subject: A seated human narrator gestures to two listeners; behind the moving hand, a soft ochre vignette shows a small animal travelling beneath a crescent Moon, clearly separate from the present ground.

name: Constellations
subject: Seven ivory stars form a loose animal-like pattern across ultramarine darkness, joined by a few fine ochre lines; unrelated background stars remain unconnected.

name: Calendar
subject: A human observer crouches beside four small groups of counting pebbles and incised tally strokes on a natural stone, beneath a repeated star pattern shown at four seasonal positions around a single horizon.

name: Wonder
subject: A small human figure stands on the hooked shore with head tipped far back and both arms gently open beneath a vast cluster of luminous stars; the upward gaze dominates.

name: Question
subject: One human figure extends an open palm toward a small bright Moon while turning an expectant face toward another person; the other person's hand pauses above the empty space between them.

name: Lunar rhythm
subject: Two matching views of the same hooked shore profile show calm water beneath a full Moon in the upper view and a quarter Moon with exactly half its disk lit in the lower view. Each view contains exactly two clear static horizontal water-level marks against the same rock face: widely separated high and low levels for the full Moon, closely spaced high and low levels for the quarter Moon; no surf or wave-height difference carries the comparison.

name: Lunar hypothesis
subject: A human observer points one hand toward the pale Moon and the other toward two tidal bands on the familiar hooked shore; one fine tentative ochre arc joins those observed features.

name: Spring-tide prediction
subject: Beside the familiar shore, a person sets two pale dry ochre marks far apart on a rock face while indicating an outlined future full Moon above a short pebble count; the present sea remains between the marks.

name: Observed spring tide
subject: At the same marked shore, one observer compares a clear dark high-water stain with the newly exposed low-water edge below it; the widely separated ochre marks now align with those two observed levels beneath a full Moon.

name: Shared discovery
subject: Three people stand at the same marked tidal rock; one indicates the high-water stain and low-water edge while another compares the pebble record and a third looks between the evidence and Moon.

name: Night vision
subject: A nocturnal furred animal's large forward eyes reflect pale moonlight above a dark branch, with its whiskered face and the branch still readable in a nearly black jade setting.

name: Pigment
subject: Three small wet daubs of ochre, coral and dark mineral color sit on a flat natural stone beside a crushed mineral fragment and a short watery smear.

name: Cave painting
subject: The established sea cave's dry pale upper wall bears one simple ochre animal outline and a hand stencil, with a human hand adding a broad mark; the dark wave-washed entrance remains below.

name: Imagined beast
subject: On the same dry cave wall, an ochre painted creature combines a long-tailed mammal body, branching antlers and feathered wings in one impossible silhouette; a small painter's hand remains at the edge.

name: Echo
subject: A lone human calls inside the established sea cave; one pale sound arc travels toward the curved dry wall and a fainter matching arc returns toward the caller, with the sea visible through the lower opening.

name: Song
subject: One human singer in the dry upper cave chamber releases a repeating sequence of three broad pale sound arcs, with the last arc rising and the singer's hand marking a gentle pulse.

name: Chorus
subject: Three human singers of different heights face inward on the dry cave ledge, their mouths open and three separate pale sound ribbons meeting in one repeating arc above them.

name: Painted sky
subject: The same dry pale cave wall carries a bold ultramarine patch filled with oversized ochre stars, an impossible coral spiral and a pale crescent; a painted handprint marks the lower edge.

name: Teaching
subject: An older person traces the familiar Moon-and-tide pattern in sand beside the marked shore while two younger listeners follow the hand; their faces and hands form a close triangle around the evidence.

name: New question
subject: A young learner lifts an open hand toward a different star beyond the Moon-and-tide pattern in the sand while an older teacher pauses and turns to follow the new direction.

name: Remembered song
subject: One younger singer repeats a three-arc pale vocal pattern; behind the singer sits a faint matching outline of an earlier group of singers and the same three arcs, without ghostly faces.

name: Changed song
subject: A young singer repeats the first two ivory arcs of the inherited vocal phrase, then sends its third arc into a distinct rising coral curl; a faint old third arc stays lower behind it.

name: Children's chorus
subject: Three children of visibly different small heights sing together on the cave's dry ledge, sharing the inherited two ivory arcs and the new rising coral ending; a taller adult listens at the far edge.

name: Dormant seeds
subject: Three intact dark-coated seeds rest protected beneath a curled dry leaf and a thin layer of cold soil, while a pale frost edge lies above them; no root has emerged.

name: Scattered seeds
subject: Several familiar dark-coated seeds lie well separated across new ochre ground, with one near an animal footprint and another beneath a distant fruit branch; none has sprouted yet.

name: Young grove
subject: Four fresh jade saplings of differing heights establish on an open ochre slope, with visible seed coats at one root and clear space between their small crowns.

name: Forest beyond the horizon
subject: A near grove releases a few small winged seeds toward a distant green ridge where additional young tree crowns disappear beyond the circle's far curve; a small open human hand remains low at the edge.
